_comment: PRESCRIPTIVE declaration: privileges that must NEVER be held, whatever the
live database currently says. This is the complement of
db-grants-manifest.json, which is DESCRIPTIVE — that file is generated with
`audit-db-grants.mjs --write` from a live database, so it records whatever
is there, including a control that has been silently undone.
Why this file exists. Migration 20260522000200_audit_log_revoke_via_definer
(C13 / OWASP A04-2) revokes UPDATE/DELETE on the immutable audit tables from
the application role and exposes the two sanctioned mutations as SECURITY
DEFINER routines (audit_log_tenant_migrate, audit_log_purge).
scripts/bootstrap-rds-roles.mjs then ran a table-blind
`GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES ... TO passwd_app`, which
re-granted exactly what the migration had revoked — and because the script is
documented as convergent and re-runnable, every convergence run reopened it.
The descriptive manifest had been regenerated against that state, so the grant
audit reported OK and the loss was invisible.
Two consumers, and BOTH are required for the control to hold:
1. scripts/bootstrap-rds-roles.mjs re-applies these REVOKEs after its
blanket grant, so convergence cannot leave them granted.
2. scripts/audit-db-grants.mjs fails when a denied privilege is held live,
AND when db-grants-manifest.json lists one — so `--write` against a
broken database can no longer launder the breakage into the expected set.
Adding an entry here is a policy decision. Removing one means deciding the
role may hold that privilege directly; say why in the PR.

denied.reason: Immutable audit trail (C13 / OWASP A04-2). The two sanctioned mutations are the SECURITY DEFINER routines audit_log_tenant_migrate (tenant merge, src/auth.ts) and audit_log_purge (retention GC + /api/maintenance/purge-audit-logs). No production code path issues a direct UPDATE/DELETE.
The tamper-evidence anchors for the audit chain. An app role that can rewrite anchors can also re-anchor forged history, which removes the detection the HMAC chain exists to provide.

Append-only routing history (SC11 / #743). The only application path that touches this table is the sign-in auto-registration writer, which needs INSERT and nothing else — no SELECT, which is why the writer issues a raw INSERT with no RETURNING. Granting SELECT back would hand an application compromise the read side of every tenant's claim-routing history; granting UPDATE or DELETE would make the record editable by the one role an attacker actually reaches. A BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger also refuses, but it is defeated by the table owner and is not the bound: this ACL is.

External review finding (20260731170000_tenant_claim_events_hardening): no application code path issues UPDATE or DELETE against tenant_claims — the only writes are findOrCreateTenantForClaim's nested `claims: { create: … }` and the operator CLI's own privileged connection, neither of which runs as passwd_app. Re-granting either would let a compromised app role reassign or revoke a claim's routing directly, bypassing the tenant_claim_events row that operation is supposed to leave — the exact evidence-destroying shape SC11 exists to close for the CLI's own writers. SELECT and INSERT stay granted: the sign-in path still needs to look up and create claim rows.

The outbox worker drains audit_outbox into audit_logs and has no business with claim routing. Listed prescriptively rather than left merely un-granted: absence alone is enforced only by the DESCRIPTIVE manifest, which `audit-db-grants.mjs --write` regenerates from whatever the database currently holds.

This table exists to OUTLIVE retention, so the retention GC must never reach it. That makes 'let the GC clean this up too' the single most predictable future change against it — arriving as a migration granting DELETE plus a manifest regeneration, both of which the descriptive manifest alone would accept. Removing this entry is a decision to let recovery-path evidence expire; say why in the PR.

The outbox worker drains audit_outbox into audit_logs and has no business resolving or mutating tenant-claim routing. Listed prescriptively (20260731170000) rather than left merely un-granted, matching the same table's tenant_claim_events entry above: absence alone is enforced only by the descriptive manifest, which `--write` regenerates from whatever the database currently holds.

The retention GC sweeps expired rows on tables that opt into it; tenant_claims is not one of them, and this table's routing correctness (which tenant a claim resolves to right now) must not be touched by a background sweep. Listed prescriptively (20260731170000) for the same reason as every other entry naming this role: absence alone is not provable from the descriptive manifest.
